question: A 47-year-old man, with a history of a right parotid pleomorphic adenoma, treated with surgery (extrafacial parotidectomy) 6 months ago, who came to our clinic because he presented pain during the mastication with sweating and reddening of the skin of the preauricular region. What treatment would be the one of choice?

options.opa: Total parotidectomy enlarged when suspicion of tumor recurrence.

analysis: The symptoms of pain during mastication with sweating and reddening of the skin in the preauricular region in a patient with a history of parotid pleomorphic adenoma raise concern for Frey syndrome, also known as gustatory sweating. This condition occurs due to aberrant reinnervation of the sweat glands by postganglionic parasympathetic fibers intended for salivary glands. The treatment of choice for Frey syndrome is injection of intradermal botulinum toxin, which helps in reducing sweating by blocking the release of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction.
